courses.subject: DPET
courses.title: Drug Metabolism
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. Introduction to the use of concepts, chemistry, enzymology, and techniques in drug metabolism for the design and development of safe and effective therapeutic agents.

courses.subject: DPET
courses.title: Advanced Clinical Pharmacy
courses.description: Discussions, workshops, and lectures to develop the student's skills and abilities to make therapeutic recommendations, utilize drug literature, educate patients and health professionals, and record observations, plans, and actions in a problem-oriented record.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 3 total credits. 3 total completions.

courses.subject: DPET
courses.title: Quantitative Methods in Clinical Research
courses.description: Required preparation, introductory biostatistics or general statistics. Graduate standing or permission of the instructor. This course reviews statistical concepts and discusses the most commonly used statistical methods for analysis of data from clinical studies or research experiments. Students will analyze problem datasets using SAS.

courses.subject: DPET
courses.title: Experimental Design Considerations in Clinical Research
courses.description: Course provides an overview of clinical trials methodology, focusing primarily on designs of (and common flaws in) clinical drug trials and nonclinical research experiments intended to answer clinical questions.

courses.subject: DPET
courses.title: PK Module 1: Pharmacokinetic Concepts and Applications
courses.description: Required preparation, elementary calculus; students without prior coursework in pharmacology/pharmacokinetics are encouraged to discuss their backgrounds with the module coordinator for recommendations of introductory work. Module is an introduction to pharmacokinetic theory, mathematical model development, and data analysis. Assumes basic knowledge of human physiology, drug administration and action, and calculus.

courses.subject: DPET
courses.title: PK: Module 2: Pharmacodynamic Concepts and Applications
courses.description: This course is an introduction to pharmacodynamics from a modeling and simulation perspective. Students will build upon the material introduced in Module 1 and apply data analysis techniques to dynamics data.

source.text: DPET 854. | 1.25 Credits. | Pre- or corequisite, DPET 853 .

courses.subject: DPET
courses.title: PK Module 3: Population PK/PD Analysis
courses.description: This course is an introduction to population pharmacokinetic and pharmacodyanmic modeling techniques, including theory and application.

courses.subject: DPET
courses.title: PK Module 4: Advanced PK/PD Modeling
courses.description: This course covers a series of advanced pharmacokinetics/pharmacodynamics (PK/PD) modeling concepts and techniques, fundamental elements towards systems pharmacology, and methodology of developing mechanism-based PK/PD models in drug development.

source.text: DPET 858. | 2 Credits. | Pre- or corequisite, DPET 857 .

courses.subject: DPET
courses.title: Precision Therapeutics Through Genomics
courses.description: Evidence-based medicine and the use of clinical practice guidelines is evolving to include application of genomic information to target drug therapies for patients. This course reviews the principles and applications of genomics to therapeutics and studies examples where this field is impacting therapeutic decisions in a variety of disease states.
